context_requirements: Tumor cells must be actively angiogenic or hypoxia-responsive for direct HIF/VEGF pathway effects.
Endothelial cells are the primary target of angiogenesis inhibitors; tumor-cell transcriptional responses are secondary and often weak.
HPGDS/HRH1 expression may be required for direct effects of some drugs in this class.
Cell lines grown in standard monolayer culture lack the stromal/endothelial compartment needed for full antiangiogenic response.
falsifiers: No change in HIF1A, VEGFA, or other hypoxia/angiogenesis markers at 24 h in any line.
Strong, uniform proliferation_down or apoptosis across all nine lines at 6 h, which would suggest a nonspecific cytotoxic mechanism rather than angiogenesis inhibition.
No difference in response between lines with high versus low HIF1A/VEGFA baseline expression.
Upregulation of endothelial-specific genes in tumor cell lines, which would be inconsistent with the expected tumor-cell response.

evidence.supports: IL6-STAT3-HIF signaling and response to the angiogenesis inhibitor sunitinib in ovarian clear cell cancer.
Semaphorin 3A is an endogenous angiogenesis inhibitor that blocks tumor growth and normalizes tumor vasculature.
Acquired resistance to the VEGF inhibitor bevacizumab involves stromal EGFR/FGFR upregulation and vascular remodeling.
A gold(I) phosphine complex acts as a TrxR-inhibiting antiproliferative agent and angiogenesis inhibitor.
Semaphorin-3B is an angiogenesis inhibitor inactivated by furin-like pro-protein convertases.
